limits: References are supplied labels, not a musician-audited gold set.
Seven song groups, short excerpts, all with empty key signatures; no held-out generalization claim.
Primary metric is sequence edit error on pitch plus rational duration, with matching ties merged. Includes rests.
Chord score measures ordered root, kind, bass and explicit extensions; chord timing is not scored.
No full notation, voice alignment, repeat-playback, lyric or accidental-display fidelity metric.
Missing or unparseable outputs count as all reference events deleted; their unparsed insertions cannot be counted.
An edit error rate can exceed 100 percent; it is not accuracy.
No correction-time study or calibrated confidence thresholds yet.
Latency includes per-image Audiveris startup, excludes neural load time; some runs overlapped, so do not compare speed as controlled performance.
Transcoda canonical header/terminator restoration changes no pitches or durations. Raw outputs are retained.
No weights trained, no labels sent to inference, no paid API calls.

decision.argument: Find sources on recognition of low-resolution single-staff music excerpts, constrained decoding to prevent repeated note generation, and chord-symbol recognition with editable kern export and consistent melody/chord transposition.
decision.why: Data and baselines are already inspected. Enlarged Audiveris has the best measured melody error rate on the pilot (0.6692), but misses 30 of 38 chords; greedy Transcoda produces 527 insertions. Sources can inform a small experiment targeting these distinct failures before spending the four-worker budget.
decision.hypothesis: Image preprocessing plus separate chord recognition, or constrained neural decoding, may address the observed failures more effectively than unrestricted greedy transcription.
decision.expected_observation: Relevant source IDs describing practical methods and their limitations, sufficient to select and read at least one source before assigning an experiment.

decision.why: The enlarged baseline recovers substantial melody but only 8 of 38 pilot chords. The format audit identifies unpromoted text as a plausible integration failure. Holding melody fixed isolates whether chord OCR and structured conversion recover useful information within the four-experiment budget; timing and musician review remain unresolved.
decision.hypothesis: Some missing chords are legible image text that can be recovered through a separate constrained recognition stage without changing melody transcription.
decision.expected_observation: More than eight correctly matched pilot chords and lower chord edit error, with unchanged melody error; failure to improve would argue that text recognition or symbol interpretation, rather than harmony export alone, is the bottleneck.

decision.why: The parent reduced measured chord error from 30/38 to 25/38, but melody error rose to 100% and none of seven files parsed. Its missing melody dependency makes integration repair more informative than further OCR tuning. Three experiments remain. The parent executed successfully and was evaluated, so this is an improve branch; the previous debug request was rejected. Preserve the baseline as the stronger measured melody comparator.
decision.hypothesis: Fresh melody recognition plus independently validated serialization can recover the baseline's melody performance while retaining some of the parent's measured chord improvement.
decision.expected_observation: Parseability increases and melody error falls below the parent's 100%; chord error remains near 25/38. Failure to obtain parseable outputs or a melody improvement would falsify this integration approach within the available runtime. Even success would leave full-dataset accuracy, chord timing and musician acceptance unresolved.

decision.expected_observation: Either verified GTK resolution enables a real MusicXML export and seven evaluable integrated predictions, or the bounded preflight exposes a specific remaining blocker. Any musical improvement must be established by subsequent protected evaluation.

last_observation.summary: GTK native loading succeeded after rootless extraction of Debian 13 arm64 packages: libgtk-3-0t64 and libgtk-3-common 3.24.49-3, with libglib2.0-0t64 2.84.4-3~deb13u5. A fresh Python process loaded libgtk-3.so.0 and queried its runtime version. System installation was blocked by apt lock-directory permissions. The export wrapper then raised subprocess.TimeoutExpired after its remaining 3.4308305588069743 seconds; the original 240-second deadline expired at 240.016 seconds. No MusicXML export or kern predictions were produced. This verifies native loading through ctypes, not successful Java/Audiveris integration; no subsequent native blocker was established. Existing Java 25/Audiveris 5.11 configuration, OCR thresholds and melody conversion were retained. All seven required predictions remain missing and count as failures. Complete-output parsing and actual-output major-second transposition checks for melody, chord roots and slash basses remain untested. Chord timing remains unaudited. No musical improvement or regression rate was measured; the transcription goal remains unmet.
